title: Restore the path from symptom to request evidence
description: Choose the instrumentation change that restores missing identity. Storage time and dashboard count cannot recover context that was never recorded.

stages.label: Resource identity
stages.detail: A stable service name and version identify the producer.

stages.label: Trace propagation
stages.detail: Request context survives the process or messaging boundary.

stages.label: Span continuity
stages.detail: The affected operation joins or links to the distributed request.

stages.label: Structured log context
stages.detail: The log carries matching trace and span identifiers.

stages.label: Metric exemplar
stages.detail: An aggregate measurement can point to a representative trace.

stages.label: Deployment marker
stages.detail: The affected service version is explicit rather than inferred by time.

incidents.label: Queue boundary
incidents.detail: A worker failure appears in metrics, but the job span is disconnected from the enqueue request.
incidents.symptom: Failed jobs rose after a traffic spike.

incidents.label: Orphan error log
incidents.detail: A structured error names the service, but it carries no trace or span fields.
incidents.symptom: An error message cannot be tied to a representative failed request.

incidents.label: Unknown service version
incidents.detail: The request is traced, but resource identity falls back and no release marker is attached.
incidents.symptom: The trace is visible, but ownership and the responsible release are ambiguous.

incidents.label: Metric-to-trace gap
incidents.detail: The latency histogram changed, but no exemplar points from the aggregate to a request trace.
incidents.symptom: The p99 moved, but operators must guess which traces represent it.

repairs.label: Propagate context and link the worker
repairs.detail: Carry trace context in message metadata and create a linked or appropriately parented consumer span.
repairs.consequence: The worker operation can be reached from the request path while preserving the asynchronous relationship.

repairs.label: Inject trace fields into logs
repairs.detail: Record the active TraceId and SpanId in the OpenTelemetry log fields.
repairs.consequence: The error event can point to the exact request and operation that emitted it.

repairs.label: Declare service resource identity
repairs.detail: Set stable service namespace, name, and version attributes at the producing resource.
repairs.consequence: Signals now identify the owning service and affected release without timestamp guessing.

repairs.label: Attach trace context as an exemplar
repairs.detail: Preserve a representative trace reference on the relevant metric measurement.
repairs.consequence: The aggregate change can lead directly to a concrete request trace.

repairs.label: Keep the same data for longer
repairs.detail: Increase storage time without changing instrumentation or propagated context.
repairs.consequence: The same disconnected evidence remains available for longer; no missing identifier is recreated.
